lede: An AI receptionist is software that answers your business phone with a voice agent. blocks.h2: AI receptionist vs virtual receptionist vs auto attendant.
blocks.intro: The three terms get used as if they meant the same thing. They do not. One is a menu, one is a team of people and one is software that holds a conversation. Knowing which is which matters, because they are priced and run differently.

items.title: Auto attendant: a phone menu
items.body: The caller presses a key or says a department name and the call is routed. It follows fixed rules. It does not understand an open question, and it does not take down what the caller needs.

items.title: Virtual receptionist: a human service
items.body: People at an outside company answer in your business name, take messages, book appointments and transfer calls. It is typically billed by the minute or by the call, within the hours and scripts you agree on.

items.title: AI receptionist: a voice agent
items.body: Software that holds a spoken conversation. It answers common questions from the information you give it, takes messages, books into a calendar you connect, routes calls and passes the caller to a person under rules you set.

items.title: AI answering service and AI voice agent
items.body: More names for the same category. The first usually means message taking and after-hours cover. The second is the broader term, also written as AI phone agent, and covers agents that place outbound calls as well.

items.title: A blend of AI and people
items.body: Some services put an AI agent on the first answer and human receptionists behind it for the calls it hands over. Ask which parts of a quote are software and which are people, because they are priced differently.

items.title: How to tell which you need
items.body: If callers only need the right department, a phone menu is enough. If most calls need judgement, use people. If most calls are the same few requests, an AI receptionist with a clear handover to a person fits.

blocks.eyebrow: What it can and cannot do
blocks.h2: What an AI phone receptionist can and cannot do.
blocks.intro: An AI receptionist is good at the routine parts of a call and poor at the parts that need judgement. What matters is where one ends and the other begins for your callers.

items.title: Answer and route calls
items.body: It picks up on the lines and during the hours you choose, asks what the caller needs and sends the call to the right person or queue. Routing follows rules you set once.

items.title: Take messages
items.body: It records who called, their number and what they asked for. Connected to the CRM, the message lands on the caller's record with a callback task for the owner, not in a voicemail box.

items.title: Book appointments
items.body: Working as an AI appointment setter, it offers open times from a calendar you connect and books the slot. It knows only the availability and the booking rules you give it.

items.title: Answer common questions
items.body: Hours, location, services, what to bring. It answers from the information you provide. A sound setup has it say when it does not know, then offer a person or a callback.

items.title: What it cannot do
items.body: It does not exercise judgement. Complaints, exceptions, pricing commitments, upset callers and unusual requests belong with a person. It can also mishear names and numbers, so it needs a step that confirms the details back to the caller.

items.title: Hand over to a person
items.body: The handover is the part to design first: the caller asks for a person, the topic is on your list, or the agent is unsure. The call transfers with a summary of what was said so far.

blocks.h2: Choosing an AI receptionist for small business teams.
blocks.intro: A demo shows the easy call. These are the points that separate one option from another once real callers are on the line. The list works with any vendor, whether or not you buy through Stacktik.

items.title: Your phone system
items.body: Check how it takes calls from the system you already use: forwarded from your main number, on its own number, or as a step in your existing call flow. Replacing the phone system is a separate decision.

items.title: Your CRM and calendar
items.body: Ask what it writes to the CRM after each call, and whether it does so directly or through a connector. A call that leaves no record means someone on your team types it in later.

items.title: The handover
items.body: Ask how a transfer to a person works, what happens when nobody picks up and what happens outside business hours. Hear it on a test call with your own scenarios, not on a slide.

items.title: Languages and recordings
items.body: Check the languages it handles, including English and French if your callers need both, where recordings and transcripts are stored, and what callers are told about recording and about speaking with an AI.

items.title: Pricing structure
items.body: Plans are commonly built from a monthly subscription, a usage charge by the minute or by the call, phone numbers and sometimes a setup fee. Ask how the bill changes in a busy month.

items.title: Control after launch
items.body: Check who can change the greeting, the answers and the rules without going back to the vendor, and whether you can read transcripts and listen to calls to hear what the agent said.

items.body: We connect the agent to your phone system and CRM. Each call creates or updates a record, with the message or summary attached, an owner assigned and the next step set as a task.

items.body: We set what the agent answers, what it never answers, when it transfers and to whom, and what happens when nobody picks up. A person on your team approves what matters, such as quotes and exceptions.

items.title: Tested, trained, handed over
items.body: We place test calls for the common requests and the awkward ones before the agent takes real calls. Your team is trained on the setup, and the handover notes say how each piece runs and who to call.

platforms.h2: The platforms an AI receptionist sits between.
platforms.intro: An AI receptionist works between a phone system and a CRM. These are the phone, contact-centre, CRM and AI platforms we set up or can source. The proposal names which fit you, and our relationship with each.

faq.a: An AI receptionist is software that answers business phone calls with a voice agent, in place of a keypad menu or a person. It greets the caller, answers common questions from information you provide, takes messages, books appointments, routes calls and hands over to a person under rules you set. Vendors sell the same thing under several names, including AI voice agent.

faq.q: How much does an AI receptionist cost?
faq.a: It depends on the vendor's plan and on how many calls you take, so there are no figures on this page. Plans are commonly built from a monthly subscription plus usage by the minute or by the call, with phone numbers and sometimes a setup fee. Stacktik's proposal shows the monthly software cost of each option, and our implementation as a fixed fee quoted in writing before work starts.

faq.q: Is an AI virtual receptionist a person or software?
faq.a: Software, in most cases. The term is used two ways: as another name for an AI receptionist, and for a blended service where an AI agent answers first and people at an answering service take the calls it hands over. Ask which one you are being quoted, because the pricing and the handover differ. A human-only service is a different purchase, and sometimes the better one.

faq.q: How do I choose an AI answering service?
faq.a: Start from your calls, not from a demo. List what callers ask for, which requests need a person and what has to be written to the CRM. Then check each option against your phone system, your CRM and calendar, its handover to people, the languages you need and how the bill changes with call volume. Stacktik puts two or three options on a written proposal with the monthly cost of each.

faq.q: How do you set up an AI receptionist?
faq.a: In this order: a free call about your calls and tools, a written proposal with a shortlist and costs, the purchase if you want us to handle it, the connection to your phone system and CRM, written rules for answers and handover, then test calls and team training before it takes real calls. You keep the tools you own unless the proposal justifies a change in writing.

faq.q: What should I check when buying an AI receptionist in Canada?
faq.a: Check whether it answers in English and French, where call recordings and transcripts are stored, and what callers are told about recording and about speaking with an AI.
